title: Air Speed Indicator and Machmeter
src: R.K. Bali — Air Navigation, Part II Ch 3

3.q: A pitot tube covered by ice which blocks the ram air inlet will affect the following instrument(s):

o: ISA at the height the aircraft is flying

13.q: A white arc on an ASI indicates:
o: safe speed on approach to land
with flaps extended in landing position
at which the flight controls can be fully deflected
not to be exceeded except in still air and with caution
continue to indicate the speed applicable at the time of the blockage

20.q: Dynamic pressure sensed by a pitot tube:
o: is not affected by the density of the surrounding air
instrument error, position error, compressibility error and manoeuvre induced error
instrument error, position error, density error and manoeuvre induced error
position, density, instrument, compressibility, manoeuvre induced
indicated speed and altitude, using a speed indicator equipped with an altimeter-type aneroid
an ordinary airspeed indicator scaled for Mach number instead of knots
a kind of echo sounder comparing the velocity of sound with indicated speed
true airspeed (TAS) divided by the local speed of sound
equivalent airspeed (EAS) divided by the local speed of sound
indicated airspeed (IAS) divided by the local speed of sound
a direct function of temperature; it varies in proportion to the square root of the absolute temperature
the ratio of the aircraft true airspeed to the sonic velocity at the altitude considered
the ratio of the aircraft conventional airspeed to the sonic velocity at the altitude considered
stick at the Mach number at the time of blockage
increase no matter what the actual Mach number
speed indicated on the autothrottle control box, versus temperature
speed indicated on the autothrottle control box, versus altitude
maximum speed in VMO operation, versus altitude
initially by the MMO, then by the VMO below a certain flight level
by the VMO in still air
an increase in the dynamic pressure

56.q: The lower and upper limits of the green arc on an ASI are:

o: The IAS will be too high when descending.
The IAS will be too low when accelerating.
The IAS will be too low at all times.
VLE at the lower end and VLO at the upper end.
VSi at the lower end and Vo at the upper end.
Vsi at the lower end and MMo at the upper end.
Decreases if the static temperature is lower than the standard temperature, increases if above.
An altimeter with a density capsule.
An AST with an altitude capsule.
A VSI with a modified scale.

92.q: If temperature decreases when flying at constant CAS at FL 200, the Machmeter indication will … and the true Mach number will …

o: The CAS of an aircraft as a fraction of the local speed of sound
The local speed of sound as a fraction of the CAS of an aircraft
The IAS of an aircraft as a fraction of the local speed of sound

ex.96: Book's key. Strictly, Mach number = TAS ÷ local speed of sound; of these options the book picks IAS.
ex.36: Book's key. Compare Q93: the Machmeter reading (from (P − S) ÷ S) has no temperature error.
ex.92: Book's key. At constant CAS and pressure altitude, (P − S) ÷ S is unchanged, so the Machmeter reading does not change; since TAS and the speed of sound both vary with √T, the true Mach number should not change either.
ex.5: Book note: It will be correct even if you accelerate or decelerate but not if you climb / descend.
ex.8: Book note: More prone to stalling because of low power setting and low speed.
ex.9: Book note: Altimeter will freeze and ASI will Under - read
ex.10: Book note: Correction for compressibility error is always negative. (subtracted)
